chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: Watching Duke and Strayhorn play together by day
summary: Collins and Jimmy Jones watched Ellington and Strayhorn play the auditorium piano as interchangeable partners.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But any way, that was one of the things. And used to have such a marvelous time. Duke and Stray Horn before the show -- see, we'd do the show at night, but during the day Duke and Stray Horn would go to the auditorium and they would just play, see. It was interchangeable. He just had this pianist, two pianists here, and they would just play it. So Jimmie Jones and I would always be there, and listen, and some great things were happening. Duke and Billy had such a great rapport, musically and otherwise, you know, it was just a beautiful thing to see. It was just-- I don't think I'll ever have any experiences like that again in life. Because I enjoyed just being there. It was -- and me feeling the way that I do about chords, you know, and to hear this was just something else.
